content_voiceover: This slide compares the four major prognostic scoring systems used for peripheral T-cell lymphoma, and understanding their overlapping risk factors is exam-relevant. The standard International Prognostic Index, the IPI, applies to all patients and uses age over sixty, elevated LDH, ECOG performance status two through four, stage three or four, and more than one extranodal site, with zero or one points defining low risk and four or five defining high risk. The age-adjusted IPI drops age and extranodal involvement, using only stage, LDH, and performance status for patients sixty and under. The Prognostic Index for PTCL-unspecified, or PIT, swaps out extranodal involvement for bone marrow involvement, alongside age, LDH, and performance status. A modified PIT further refines this by dropping bone marrow involvement and adding Ki-67 greater than or equal to eighty percent, reflecting proliferation rate as a prognostic driver specific to PTCL biology. Finally, the T-cell score from the International T-cell Lymphoma Project uses stage, performance status, low albumin, and a high absolute neutrophil count. The common thread is that performance status and LDH or a proliferation marker consistently predict outcome, while the specific fourth or fifth variable is what differentiates each index and reflects how PTCL biology diverges from B-cell lymphomas.
keypoints: IPI: age >60, LDH, ECOG 2-4, stage III/IV, >1 extranodal site
Age-adjusted IPI (<=60y): stage, LDH, performance status only
PIT (PTCL-U): age, LDH, ECOG, plus bone marrow involvement
Modified PIT: swaps bone marrow for Ki-67 >=80%
T-cell score: stage, ECOG, low albumin, high ANC
keypoint_voiceover: Five scoring systems, one pattern: performance status and LDH show up almost everywhere. The IPI adds extranodal sites, the PIT swaps that for bone marrow involvement, and the modified PIT swaps marrow for Ki-67 over eighty percent, capturing proliferation. The T-cell score instead uses albumin and absolute neutrophil count. If a question asks which index is PTCL-specific and uses Ki-67, that's the modified PIT.
